notes: YouTube TV (2026-10-05, 'Youtube TV has a LOT of live TV and it's not on my live tab'): the Live tab reads the guide page, tv.youtube.com/live - a ytu-epg-row per channel (its name, logo and browse/UC... id) and a ytu-epg-airing per program (the start time as text, 10 px a minute of width, is-live_ on the one on now, the program title and a line of rating, season/episode or date); about three and a half hours a read, YouTube TV's own guide. A tune presses the channel row's thumbnail and then 'Join live' in the page's own question (How would you like to begin watching?), which opens /watch/<id>; from another page the guide is opened first and the press follows. The watch page names the program (h1.ypc-video-title), the LIVE badge, and its controls by aria-label (Pause (k), Full screen (f), Back/Forward 15 seconds, Subtitles). The Library (recordings) and purchases follow. Library (0.3.0): tv.youtube.com/library - the person's own rows, New in your library (shows with new episodes), Most watched and Scheduled recordings (the upcoming recordings, LIVE on the ones recording now), from the page's shelves; and Recordings & purchases, the grid the header counts (1,373 on this account), read as the owned library on the owned page (the same address with ?prism=owned, which YouTube TV ignores) by scrolling until the count is reached - a show is a series, a MOVIE thumb a title, 'Purchased' kept as a badge. 2026-10-06, captions: the player's captions are kept on and read for the break watch (an ad says its brand, number and address; captions go quiet at a cut), shown only when the person picks captions in Prism's Captions menu (kept in this browser, localStorage prismCaptionsShown), hidden otherwise. The caption choice is the player's own (localStorage yt-html5-player-modules::subtitlesModuleData), not the account's. Live news and talk channels carry captions; FX's film gave none. 0.3.17 (2026-10-08): a tune to a programme that can be started over (Comedy Central's South Park) stood at YouTube TV's own question, 'How would you like to begin watching? Join live / Start from beginning', until the tune timed out and the small window was closed as empty: the script pressed the ytu-menu-item host, which takes no press. Read live on a hidden page: the option inside it (tp-yt-paper-icon-item[role=option]) does, and the channel starts. A live programme with no start-over (CNN) asks nothing, which is why the earlier tunes worked.

verified.cue: 2026-10-08, the cue was read when the page appended the data to its buffer, which runs 14 to 31 s ahead of the picture: on the marked hours a slot slid 14-24 s later fits the marked ads best (NBC Sports 79% of slot seconds inside a marked ad as read, 95% slid 24 s; NFL Network 95% and 99% at 14 s), and each slot that opens a break covered some 20 s of the show before it. Measured in the page on Food Network: buffer end at the append less the playhead = 14.0 s, the cue so placed 16:49:09.9, the player's own ad-showing mark 16:49:10.1. So each cue is posted twice: at once, marked early (what the learned detector was trained on, and an advance word of a slot), and again, held with the media time it was appended at (the buffer's end before the append), when the playhead reaches it - the sure rule's; whatever the playhead does (pause, back 10 s, catching up to live) the latest cue at or before it is the one in force. A cue with no buffer to place it by goes at once, as before.
verified.adsTray: 2026-10-06, read on both playing windows through two breaks the person saw (FX, USA): no mark at all - the player never took ad-showing, the ytu-ads-title-tray (Sponsored) stayed hidden, no Ad text, no ad requests, the stream's segments carried no emsg (SABR; the player takes its own metadata out before the append). These are the channels' own broadcast commercials and cannot be told from the page. The tray is kept as a mark for YouTube TV's own inserted ads, should one show it.
